issue_context.summary: PowerRename reportedly renames a desktop .lnk but leaves Windows treating it as an empty link or text file.
known_information: The shortcut was created with Send to desktop and renamed on PowerToys 0.70.1.
The search removed the localized '.exe - Verknüpfung' portion of the display name.
Current PowerRename uses the filesystem path and IFileOperation::RenameItem, which should preserve shortcut contents.
inferences: The apparent target loss may actually be removal of the hidden .lnk extension or may have been fixed since 0.70.1; current file properties will distinguish those cases.
issue_context.analysis: The current rename path does not edit IShellLink contents. The smallest useful evidence is a current synthetic shortcut plus before/after file type, extension, size, and target—not a broad diagnostic package.
initial_investigation: PowerRenameItem initializes the original name from SIGDN_FILESYSPATH, which includes the real filename.
PowerRenameManager performs IFileOperation::RenameItem on the IShellItem and does not intentionally modify shortcut payload.

information_gaps.information: Whether the renamed file still has the .lnk extension, nonzero size, and original Target in Properties on a current build
information_gaps.why_needed: It distinguishes lost file association/name handling from actual shortcut-content corruption.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Create a non-sensitive test shortcut, enable Explorer file-name extensions, record Properties before and after PowerRename, and state the resulting filename, type, size, and Target.

information_gaps.information: The latest PowerToys version on which the synthetic shortcut still fails
information_gaps.why_needed: The only report is from 0.70.1 and current rename code may no longer reproduce.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Retest on the latest stable release and provide the version from PowerToys About.

comment.body:
Thanks for the exact German shortcut name and replacement text. Current PowerRename renames the shell item but does not intentionally edit the shortcut target, so we need to distinguish hidden `.lnk` extension removal from actual shortcut-content corruption.

**Needed**
1. Please retest with a non-sensitive test shortcut on the latest stable PowerToys version and provide that version from About.
2. With Explorer **File name extensions** enabled, please record the shortcut's filename, file type, size, and Target in Properties before and after PowerRename.

This will determine whether the fix belongs in extension preservation, shell-item renaming, or shortcut payload handling.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve shell-link identity during localized display-name renames
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Best current hypothesis: extension-exclusion or localized display-name handling can produce a final name without .lnk, making intact shortcut bytes appear as an unknown/empty file.
plan: Add a test shortcut with a localized '- Verknüpfung' name and inspect the exact newName passed to IFileOperation.
Guarantee hidden shell-link extensions are preserved independently of the visible search/replace segment.
Verify the target, arguments, icon, and file size remain unchanged after rename.
verification: Rename synthetic .lnk files with extensions hidden and shown; verify Windows still recognizes and launches every shortcut.

confidence.rationale: The hidden-extension explanation fits the appearance, but the current code path should preserve .lnk and needs a modern reproduction.
